messages:
olivia_acme: Hey team — we've got a customer on our embedded web app hitting a hard reauth loop after MFA enrollment. Happens only in Chrome 113+ when using our iframe-based widget. They say the user completes SSO + MFA, then returns to the app and immediately gets bounced to reauth.
olivia_acme: Repro steps they sent: 1) Open product in iframe on acme.example.com 2) Click ‘Sign in with SSO’ 3) Complete IdP + authenticator prompt 4) Redirect back to app -> shows login overlay again. Intermittent, ~70% failure.

maria_support: Thanks Olivia — can you paste the browser console network log for the post-auth redirect (the call that should exchange device_jwt/session cookie)? Also which SDK version and widget config are they using?

olivia_acme: SDK v2.4.0 (iframe integration). Attaching the relevant headers they copied from devtools:

--- request -> /auth/complete ---
Cookie: session=; device_jwt=eyJhbGci...; other=...
Set-Cookie: session=eyJ...; Path=/; Secure; SameSite=Lax; HttpOnly
Set-Cookie: device_jwt=eyJ...; Path=/; Secure; SameSite=None; HttpOnly; Domain=.example.com

They also see a chrome console warning: "A cookie associated with a cross-site resource at https://auth.redwood.ai was set without the 'SameSite' attribute. It has been treated as None."

sam_engineer: Hmm. Two quick thoughts: 1) If the iframe is cross-site (auth host vs app host) Chrome will enforce SameSite rules; if a cookie returned without SameSite=None; Secure it may be blocked. 2) We also changed device_jwt rotation in v2.4 to require SameParty in some cases for nested iframes. Could be a mismatch between our Set-Cookie and the widget expecting a postMessage token.

kevin_sre: I pulled the gateway logs for the customer's org around ts 2026-02-22T18:03:12Z. I see repeated 403s on /session/validate with X-Device-Claim missing. Gateway remarks: "cookie not sent — third-party cookie blocked by user agent". Snippet:

[WARN] 18:03:12 gateway: session validate failed, user=olivia_user_123, reason=missing_cookie, ua=Mozilla/5.0 (Chrome/113.0.0)
[DEBUG] cookie_check: SameSite check failed for cookie session; request origin=https://acme.example.com

maria_support: Can you reproduce locally if you iframe our auth domain into a different origin? Also ask customer if they have any extensions or Chrome flags. We should provide a short repro they can run.

olivia_acme: They tested incognito and still hit the loop. No extensions. Only on Chrome; Safari and Firefox work fine.

sam_engineer: OK reproduce steps for us and them (to include in ticket):
1) Host a small page on http://localhost:3000 with an <iframe src="https://auth.redwood.ai/embed?widget=...">.
2) Start a session and follow SSO flow.
3) Watch network panel: confirm browser blocks Set-Cookie for session (look for "cookie blocked third-party").

Also try the workaround: set the widget to use top-level redirect for post-auth instead of direct iframe exchange. Most customers see fewer problems with that in Chrome.

olivia_acme: Customer asked for a patch instead of changing UX. Any config flags we can toggle server-side to avoid blocking?

kevin_sre: Short answer: we can't force a browser to accept third-party cookies, but we can change how the widget finalizes auth. Options:
- Use top-level navigation (window.top.location) after IdP auth so the cookie is set in a first-party context.
- Use postMessage flow where the IdP returns a one-time code to the parent and parent exchanges via fetch (first-party).
- Offer SameSite=None; Secure for the main session cookie and ensure Domain is correct (no overly broad Domain) — but if browser blocks third-party cookies policy-wide, still blocked.

maria_support: For now let's give the customer a targeted SDK patch: v2.4.1 that falls back to top-level exchange when embedded and when UA indicates Chrome >= 113 and context is cross-site. I can draft a patch note and a hotfix build.

deploy-bot: deploy request queued: patch-auth-widget v2.4.1 -> canary. Triggered by maria_support. (build id: build-4721)

sam_engineer: Also add diagnostics to logs so we surface "cookie blocked" vs "cookie present but invalid" — right now they look identical at the API layer. We should log the presence/absence of the Cookie header and the Set-Cookie result from our response pipeline.

olivia_acme: I pushed the canary to the customer's org and they tested— initial report: 80% reduction in loops when canary used. They still had two failures where the IdP did top-level redirect to a different domain before we could exchange.

maria_support: For those last cases, ask the IdP to preserve relay_state or pass the one-time code back (we can consume it on top-level). Sending a small snippet for customers to implement as fallback:

```js
// fallback on parent page
window.addEventListener('message', (e) => {
  if (e.data && e.data.oneTimeCode) {
    fetch('/exchange', {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
      body: JSON.stringify({ code: e.data.oneTimeCode })
    }).then(r => r.json()).then(console.log);
  }
});
```

maria_support: Action items — assign:
- sam_engineer: add enhanced cookie diagnostics + UA-based fallback logic (PR)
- kevin_sre: monitor canary logs for "cookie blocked" counts and rollback threshold
- maria_support: ship v2.4.1 hotfix and share migration notes with customer
- olivia_acme: coordinate with customer's IdP to preserve relay_state where possible

kevin_sre: Logged a short-term alert: if >10% of auths in org X fail due to missing cookie over 15m, notify eng-sre.

olivia_acme: Thanks all — customer will test full day tomorrow and report. I'll update thread with any new failures + console exports.

maria_support: Thanks — marking this as escalated. Will keep the canary open and aim to release stable in 48 hours if metrics look good. :thumbsup:
